# lsastrat

**Stratification and inequality metrics for large-scale assessment (LSA)
data.**

`lsastrat` computes the educational-stratification quantities that
PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS researchers normally hand-assemble, and returns them as
first-class objects with correct **plausible-value pooling** (Rubin’s
rules) and **replicate-weight variance** (BRR/Fay, JK2, JK1):

- [`social_gradient()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/social_gradient.md)
  — the socio-economic achievement gradient (slope, strength = *R*² ×
  100, curvature).
- [`segregation_index()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/segregation_index.md)
  — school segregation indices (Dissimilarity, Gorard’s S, isolation,
  Hutchens, Theil’s H, mutual information) with a two-stage clustered
  bootstrap and **finite-sample bias correction**.
- [`ieop()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/ieop.md) — the
  Ferreira–Gignoux decomposition of inequality of educational
  opportunity.

It also **decomposes** these quantities (between/within-school variance,
Shapley decomposition of inequality of opportunity, Oaxaca–Blinder gap
decomposition), **compares** them across countries/subgroups
([`lsa_by()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_by.md),
[`equity_scatter()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/equity_scatter.md)),
and runs PV/weight-aware **specification-curve (multiverse)** analyses
([`lsa_multiverse()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_multiverse.md)),
with base and `ggplot2` (`autoplot()`) graphics throughout. For models
beyond the built-in estimators,
[`lsa_model()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_model.md)
fits **any** model (`lm`, `glm`, multilevel `lme4::lmer`) to
plausible-value outcomes with replicate-weight inference, and
[`lsa_trend()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_trend.md)
compares a quantity across assessment cycles with the linking error
folded in.

General LSA packages (`EdSurvey`, `intsvy`, `BIFIEsurvey`, `RALSA`,
OECD’s `Rrepest`) handle plausible values and replicate weights but
expose only generic estimators (means, regression, correlation); none
emits these stratification quantities as labelled outputs, and a
replicate-weight loop (even a user-supplied one, as in
`BIFIEsurvey::BIFIE.by`) structurally cannot estimate the finite-sample
bias of segregation indices — that requires re-sampling students within
schools, which is why `lsastrat` nests a clustered bootstrap inside the
Rubin pooling. `lsastrat` fills that gap and is designed to sit
*alongside* those engines.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("kevisc/lsastrat")
```

## Example

All examples use the bundled, fully simulated `pisa_mini` data set.

``` r

library(lsastrat)
data(pisa_mini)

reps <- paste0("W_FSTURWT", 1:64)

social_gradient(
  pisa_mini,
  achievement = paste0("PV", 1:10, "MATH"),
  escs = "ESCS", weight = "W_FSTUWT", repweights = reps
)
#> Socio-economic achievement gradient
#>   SES index: ESCS   |   10 plausible value(s)   |   n = 2048
#>   Variance:  BRR, 64 replicate weights (+ PV imputation); t reference
#> 
#> 
#>           Estimate Std.Error     t    df       p
#> slope       41.357     1.831 22.59 399.4 2.1e-73
#> strength    20.189     1.799 11.22 389.1 1.7e-25
#> curvature    1.025     1.597  0.64 406.7 5.2e-01
#> 
#> slope = score points per 1 unit of ESCS; strength = % variance explained (R^2 x 100)
```

``` r

# social segregation by immigrant background, bias-corrected bootstrap variance
segregation_index(
  pisa_mini, unit = "school_id", group = "IMMIG", weight = "W_FSTUWT",
  variance = "bootstrap", n_boot = 199, boot_seed = 1
)
#> Segregation indices (social segregation)
#>   unit: school_id  |  128 units  |  3 group(s)  |  minority: first_gen
#>   Variance: clustered bootstrap (B=199, cluster=school_id), bias-corrected
#> 
#> 
#>           Estimate Std.Error     t  df       p
#> D            0.575     0.038 15.12 Inf 1.2e-51
#> S            0.550     0.041 13.41 Inf 5.1e-41
#> isolation    0.100     0.028  3.53 Inf 4.1e-04
#> Hutchens     0.359     0.037  9.70 Inf 3.0e-22
#> H            0.096     0.018  5.25 Inf 1.5e-07
#> M            0.075     0.017  4.49 Inf 7.1e-06
```

``` r

# inequality of opportunity attributable to circumstances
ieop(
  pisa_mini,
  achievement = paste0("PV", 1:10, "MATH"),
  circumstances = c("IMMIG", "parental_edu", "books"),
  weight = "W_FSTUWT", repweights = reps
)
#> Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux)
#>   10 plausible value(s)  |  n = 2048  |  3 circumstance(s): IMMIG, parental_edu, books
#>   Variance: BRR, 64 replicate weights (+ PV imputation); t reference
#> 
#> 
#>               Estimate Std.Error     t     df        p
#> iop              0.209     0.018 11.79  612.6  4.6e-29
#> iop_adj          0.206     0.018 11.58  610.7  3.7e-28
#> explained_var 1518.225   143.167 10.60 1204.1  3.5e-25
#> total_var     7253.731   228.176 31.79  517.7 8.7e-124
#> 
#> iop = share of achievement variance explained by circumstances (raw R^2, upper bound); iop_adj = df-adjusted
```

Every estimator returns an `lsastrat_estimate` object, so
[`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html),
[`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html),
[`as.data.frame()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/as.data.frame.html) and
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) work uniformly.

## Validation

The estimators are cross-validated against established implementations:
[`social_gradient()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/social_gradient.md)
reproduces
[`intsvy::pisa.reg.pv()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/intsvy/man/pisa.reg.pv.html);
the Dissimilarity and Theil’s H indices match the `segregation` package;
and [`ieop()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/ieop.md)
matches a weighted regression *R*². Beyond the test suite, a
reproducible script
([`data-raw/validate_pisa2022.R`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/data-raw/validate_pisa2022.R))
repeats these checks on the **official PISA 2022 public-use microdata**
for six education systems: slopes, standard errors and explained
variance agree with `intsvy` to better than 0.01 score points, Theil’s H
agrees with `segregation` to within 1e-6, and the between-school
variance shares recover the familiar comprehensive-vs-tracked contrast
(Finland 0.12 vs Germany 0.47).

## Getting help & contributing

Please report bugs and ask questions on the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/kevisc/lsastrat/issues). See
[CONTRIBUTING](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/CONTRIBUTING.md) and
the [Code of
Conduct](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Roadmap

Cross-fitted (sample-split) inequality of opportunity and stratified
multiverse designs are planned for future releases.

# Package index

## Estimators

First-class stratification and inequality quantities.

- [`social_gradient()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/social_gradient.md)
  : Socio-economic achievement gradient
- [`segregation_index()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/segregation_index.md)
  : School segregation indices for large-scale assessment data
- [`ieop()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/ieop.md) :
  Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux)
- [`variance_decomposition()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/variance_decomposition.md)
  : Between- and within-school variance decomposition

## General modelling

Fit arbitrary models, and compare across cycles.

- [`lsa_model()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_model.md)
  : Fit any model to plausible-value outcomes with replicate-weight
  inference
- [`lsa_trend()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_trend.md)
  : Trend across assessment cycles with linking error

## Decompositions

Attributing inequality to its sources.

- [`ieop_decompose()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/ieop_decompose.md)
  : Shapley decomposition of inequality of educational opportunity
- [`oaxaca_gap()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/oaxaca_gap.md)
  : Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition of an achievement gap

## Comparison and multiverse

Comparative and robustness analysis.

- [`lsa_by()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_by.md) :
  Run an estimator across groups (e.g. countries)
- [`equity_scatter()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/equity_scatter.md)
  : Quality-equity scatter across groups
- [`lsa_multiverse()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_multiverse.md)
  : Plausible-value / weight-aware multiverse (specification-curve)
  analysis
- [`lsa_design()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsa_design.md)
  : Bundle a survey design for reuse

## Variance engine

The shared plausible-value pooling and replicate-weight machinery.

- [`pool_pv()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/pool_pv.md)
  : Pool point estimates and variances across plausible values (Rubin's
  rules)
- [`rep_factor()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/rep_factor.md)
  : Replicate-weight variance factors

## Methods

Accessors and plots for fitted objects.

- [`print(`*`<lsastrat_estimate>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsastrat_estimate.md)
  [`summary(`*`<lsastrat_estimate>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsastrat_estimate.md)
  [`coef(`*`<lsastrat_estimate>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsastrat_estimate.md)
  [`confint(`*`<lsastrat_estimate>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsastrat_estimate.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<lsastrat_estimate>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/lsastrat_estimate.md)
  : Methods for lsastrat estimate objects
- [`tidy()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/tidy.lsastrat_estimate.md)
  [`glance()`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/tidy.lsastrat_estimate.md)
  : Tidy an lsastrat estimate
- [`autoplot(`*`<lsastrat_estimate>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/autoplot.lsastrat.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<social_gradient>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/autoplot.lsastrat.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<lsastrat_by>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/autoplot.lsastrat.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<equity_scatter>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/autoplot.lsastrat.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<lsa_multiverse>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/autoplot.lsastrat.md)
  : ggplot2 autoplot methods
- [`plot(`*`<social_gradient>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/plot.social_gradient.md)
  : Plot a socio-economic achievement gradient
- [`plot(`*`<segregation>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/plot.segregation.md)
  : Plot a school segregation profile
- [`plot(`*`<lsastrat_by>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/plot.lsastrat_by.md)
  : Forest / caterpillar plot of an estimate across groups
- [`plot(`*`<equity_scatter>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/plot.equity_scatter.md)
  : Plot a quality-equity scatter
- [`plot(`*`<lsa_multiverse>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/plot.lsa_multiverse.md)
  : Specification-curve plot
- [`plot(`*`<lsa_trend>`*`)`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/plot.lsa_trend.md)
  : Plot a cross-cycle trend

## Data

- [`pisa_mini`](https://kevisc.github.io/lsastrat/reference/pisa_mini.md)
  : Simulated PISA-like assessment data
